retrospective.summary: Retrospective section: one durable learning captured this session, distinct from the previously-documented lefthook-vs-CI discrepancy.
learningsCaptured: Three independent functions in this codebase decide whether a session log gets creation-mode leniency, and they disagree: git_hook_policy.py session's git-index check, pre_pr.py --quick's branch-relative new_session_logs() (which never actually reaches --creation-mode due to a latent bug in _prepr_session_command()), and the real CI check's committed_session_validation_modes() (exact-head-commit-only). A new session log's leniency window under the real CI check closes permanently the instant any further commit lands on top of the commit that created it, even one that never touches the log. Any session that spans more than one commit must complete its own sessionEnd honestly within the commit that creates the log, or fold that completion into whatever commit becomes the new tip before pushing, never leave it dangling across a later commit while assuming the leniency will persist. Captured to Serena memory at pr-autofix/pre-pr-quick-check-session-end-discrepancy.
